farcana.upside: The rebrand from a shooter game to an AI-compute and gaming ecosystem (March 2026) and a promised public beta of the game on the Epic Games Store in the second half of 2026 could bring new attention if it actually ships.
farcana.cheap: The token lost over 99% since its 2024 high and moved chains (Polygon to BNB Chain), so most old holders left; nobody is paying attention until the beta is real.
farcana.wrongIf: No dated public beta or working AI product by the end of December 2026, or daily trading stays under $300K.

natix-network.upside: A real product: a driving-camera data network with about 269K drivers, a Valeo partnership and quarterly token burns (110.7M burned in April 2026); another burn or a new data-buyer deal could move it.
natix-network.cheap: Small DePIN tokens are out of favour even as their revenue grows, and the project's public updates went quiet after May 2026.
natix-network.wrongIf: No progress update or burn announcement by mid-December 2026, or the price gives back this week's 13% gain as trading falls back to normal.
natix-network.vsScanner: The scanner calls it a zombie (no code since May); the business looks alive but I can't confirm any update after May, so I sit between the two.

oobit-2.upside: Oobit is a real, Tether-backed crypto payments app with launches all year (Phantom support in January, bank transfers in February, Colombia in May); stablecoin card spending is growing fast industry-wide.
oobit-2.cheap: The company is real but the token barely trades ($30K a day) and has fallen 99% since its November 2025 launch, so the market doesn't believe the token captures any of the app's value.
oobit-2.wrongIf: Trading stays under $100K a day, or the company announces no token use (fees, rewards, buybacks) by end of January 2027.
oobit-2.vsScanner: The scanner likes the 'alive' signs, but the token trades far too thinly to buy and sell safely; the company's success does not flow to the token.
